CHIEF COMPLAINT
Severe right upper arm pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
39-year-old female presents with severe right upper arm pain following a volleyball injury. Patient reports that approximately 18 hours ago (7:00 PM last evening), while attempting to spike the ball, an opponent kicked her legs from under her, causing her to fall and land on her right shoulder/arm. Pain severity is rated 9/10. Patient has been taking ibuprofen every 6 hours with minimal relief. No ice has been applied. X-ray reveals a proximal humerus fracture.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No numbness or tingling in the right arm. Physical examination notable for swelling and erythema on the right shoulder with tenderness over the right shoulder. Normal pulses. Rest of body examination normal.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Gallstones. Lumbar fusion 6 years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen every 6 hours. Pepcid.

ALLERGIES
No allergies to medicines.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Plays volleyball.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right shoulder: swelling and erythema with tenderness. Right arm: normal pulses, able to straighten elbow and bend elbow. No numbness or tingling. Rest of body examination normal.

RESULTS
X-ray of right arm demonstrates proximal humerus fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Proximal humerus fracture. These fractures typically heal without surgery. Patient will be immobilized with a long arm cast and sling. Follow-up in 2 weeks to assess for bone realignment; surgery will be considered if bones have not realigned. Prescribed Lortab 5 mg, 1-2 tablets every 6 hours as needed for pain, quantity 20. Cast to be applied by technician prior to discharge.
